$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-08-28 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 5b806f35. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v20 indexes (sub2api INDEX d4c08fda, attestor INDEX cef1d03d) built by publish-tee-images run 33158993160; the keyless signatures verify against certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market, and the Fulcio certificates embed githubWorkflowSha = the sourceCommit below. This release raises the default concurrency cap for newly connected supply accounts from 3 to 15. The old value was never reasoned about — the code comment said it was simply copied from the ent schema default — and it caused production 503s: the single serving supply account (cap 3) absorbed 98% of traffic, saturated, and hit upstream rate limits at the same second as the fallback account, leaving no schedulable account at all. First-party accounts run at 20, and a supplier's quota is indistinguishable from ours upstream, so there was no reason to cap them at a fifth of that. The real ceiling remains upstream 429s, which RateLimitService already handles. Note this constant only affects NEW connections; the existing production account was updated separately through the admin API. Earlier in this line: proof-v19 (abuse detection, shipped disabled), v18 (take-offline copy), v17 (reference-source fix + first-screen 1332KB->118KB), v16/v15 (two-sided marketplace). osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation.
